rule: docs/TREE_PLAN.md: one yard tree for every two or three houses, in back yards and at lot corners, never against a fence or a wall (zone 813 -> about 400)
written: by hand, 19 Nov 2026 (cloud session, the city-wide superchecker run from the bottom of the list). The quadrant's twenty-three builder trees go (ficus, corals, jacarandas, magnolias, four canary date palms in the back yards, queen palms and a fan palm 1.2-4.7 m from the houses); five come back on their own spots, about one for every two houses: by the patio set, the two grills, and the open south lot corners.

trees.why: the back yard with the adirondack chair and the patio set: a magnolia over the table
the back yard with the kettle grill (2.7 m off): shade over the cook
the south yard with the kettle grill (1.6 m off) and the adirondack chair beside: a jacaranda over both
the open lot corner at the south-west, 24 m from the walls: a full coral tree
the south back lot line, 15 m from the houses: an old ficus between two yards
